pronunciation: Word stress — -tion / -sion endings: stress the syllable before -tion / -sion (conviction, mission, decision, salvation, confusion)
pronunciation_detail: English words ending in -tion or -sion follow one very reliable rule: the stress falls on the syllable just before -tion / -sion. Once you know this rule, you can pronounce hundreds of long words correctly — even words you have never seen before. Vietnamese has no word stress like this, so learners often stress the wrong syllable (saying con-vic-TION or sal-va-tion with a flat rhythm), which makes the word hard to understand. conVICtion /kənˈvɪk.ʃən/ — stress VIC, not -tion. MISsion /ˈmɪʃ.ən/ — stress MIS, not -sion. deCIsion /dɪˈsɪʒ.ən/ — stress CI, not -sion. salVAtion /sælˈveɪ.ʃən/ — stress VA, not -tion. conFUsion /kənˈfjuː.ʒən/ — stress FU, not -sion. proclaMAtion /ˌprɒk.ləˈmeɪ.ʃən/ — stress MA, not -tion. Rule: find the ending -tion or -sion, then go one syllable back and stress it — say that syllable louder, longer, and higher. The ending itself is always weak and quiet: -tion sounds like /ʃən/, -sion sounds like /ʃən/ or /ʒən/. Note the exception in this lesson: Pentecost /ˈpen.tɪ.kɒst/ does not end in -tion, and its stress falls on the first syllable, PEN-te-cost. Practice: listen to the lesson audio and shadow the narrator — copy the stress on conviction, mission, decision, salvation exactly. Then read this sentence aloud twice, stressing the capital syllables: "His words brought conVICtion, and they made the deCIsion to follow Jesus, because salVAtion is God's gift to the world."

grammar.title: Phrasal verbs: come upon, fill with, speak out, stand up, pour out, break out; separable vs inseparable, with the object pronoun rule
grammar.explain:
A phrasal verb is a verb + a small word (a particle, like up, out, upon) that together have a new meaning. Pour means to tip liquid from a container; pour out means to give freely and in full measure — God poured out His Spirit. The six phrasal verbs of this lesson all come from Acts: come upon — to arrive and rest on someone: "The Holy Spirit came upon the believers." fill with — to make full of something: "God filled them with boldness." stand up — to rise to your feet: "Peter stood up and spoke." speak out — to speak boldly and openly: "Do not be afraid to speak out about Jesus." pour out — to give freely and in full measure: "God poured out His Spirit on all people." break out — to start suddenly: "Great joy broke out in the city." Separable phrasal verbs — the object can go in the middle pour out and speak out are separable: the object can go between the verb and the particle, or after the whole verb. Both are correct: "God poured out His Spirit on all people." — "God poured His Spirit out on all people." And: "They spoke out the word boldly." — "They spoke the word out boldly." Inseparable phrasal verbs — nothing goes in the middle come upon, fill with and break out are inseparable: the object must come after the whole verb, never in the middle. Say "The Spirit came upon them", never "came them upon". Say "God filled them with power", never "filled with them power". Say "Joy broke out in the city", never "broke in the city out". stand up usually takes no object at all: "Peter stood up."

The object pronoun rule — the most important rule When the object is a pronoun (it, them, him, her, us), the rule becomes strict. With a separable verb, the pronoun must go between the verb and the particle: "God poured it out on all people." — never "poured out it". "They spoke it out boldly." — never "spoke out it". With an inseparable verb, the pronoun stays after the whole verb: "The Spirit came upon them." — "God filled them with power."

Watch out: Vietnamese has no phrasal verbs, so learners often put the pronoun in the wrong place ("poured out it") or split an inseparable verb ("came them upon"). Ask two questions: (1) Can this verb split at all? (2) Is my object a pronoun? If the verb splits and the object is a pronoun, the pronoun goes in the middle — always.

reading_passage: Fifty days after Jesus rose from the dead, the day of Pentecost arrived. The believers were all together in one place in Jerusalem, waiting and praying as Jesus had told them to do. Suddenly, a sound like a mighty rushing wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting. Tongues of fire appeared and rested on each one of them. The Holy Spirit came upon them, and they were all filled with power. They began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit gave them words to speak. People from many nations were amazed, because each one heard the believers speaking in his own language. Some people were confused, but Peter stood up with the eleven apostles and spoke out boldly. He proclaimed that Jesus, whom the people had crucified, is both Lord and Christ. His words brought conviction to the crowd. They asked, "What shall we do?" Peter said, "Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit." About three thousand people were baptized that day, and the church in Jerusalem was born. Soon after this, Peter and John were arrested and threatened, and the leaders told them not to speak about Jesus anymore. But the believers did not hide. They gathered together and prayed: "Lord, give your servants boldness to speak your word." As they prayed, the place where they were gathered was shaken. They were filled with the Holy Spirit again, and they continued to speak the word of God with boldness. The same Spirit who came at Pentecost still fills God's people today, and He still gives them power to be His witnesses.

reading_comprehension.q: 1. What happened when the Holy Spirit came on the day of Pentecost?
reading_comprehension.a: The Holy Spirit came upon the believers, and they were filled with power and began to speak in other languages.

reading_comprehension.q: 2. What did Peter do when he stood up before the crowd?
reading_comprehension.a: He stood up and proclaimed that Jesus is Lord and Christ, and he called the crowd to repent and be baptized.

reading_comprehension.q: 3. What was the result of Peter's sermon?
reading_comprehension.a: About three thousand people received his word and were baptized that day.

reading_comprehension.q: 4. What did the believers do in Acts 4 after Peter and John were threatened?
reading_comprehension.a: They prayed together, asking God for boldness to speak His word, and the place where they were gathered was shaken.

reading_comprehension.q: 5. What happened after the believers prayed?
reading_comprehension.a: They were filled with the Holy Spirit again and continued to speak the word of God with boldness.

listening_questions.q: 1. What happened on the day of Pentecost?
listening_questions.a: With a sound like a mighty rushing wind, and with tongues of fire that rested on each believer. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues.

listening_questions.q: 2. What did Peter do on the day of Pentecost?
listening_questions.a: He stood up and proclaimed that Jesus, whom the people had crucified, is both Lord and Christ — and he called the people to repent and be baptized.

listening_questions.q: 3. How many people were baptized on the day of Pentecost?
listening_questions.a: About three thousand people were baptized that day.

listening_questions.q: 4. What happened when the believers prayed together in Acts 4?
listening_questions.a: The place where they were gathered together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit again.

listening_questions.q: 5. What did the believers ask God for in their prayer?
listening_questions.a: They asked God to give them boldness to speak His word, while He stretched out His hand to heal and to do signs and wonders.

listening_questions.q: 6. What did the Friend decide to do this week?
listening_questions.a: He decided to pray with a friend this week and speak out boldly about Jesus.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Word Stress — -tion / -sion
exercises.instruction: Say each word aloud. Underline (or write in capitals) the stressed syllable. Remember: in -tion / -sion words, the stress falls on the syllable just before -tion / -sion.

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Separable or Inseparable? — The Pronoun Rule
exercises.instruction: Choose the correct sentence (a or b). Think about the object pronoun rule: with a separable phrasal verb, a pronoun object goes BETWEEN the verb and the particle; with an inseparable phrasal verb, nothing goes between them.

speaking_task: Roleplay in pairs (3 minutes): Student A tells Student B what happened on the day of Pentecost, using at least 4 phrasal verbs from this lesson (come upon, fill with, stand up, speak out, pour out, break out). Student B asks two questions ('What did Peter do when he stood up?', 'What happened when the believers prayed?'). Use at least 5 vocabulary words from Section 3 and at least 3 words with -tion / -sion endings, with the stress on the right syllable (conVICtion, MISsion, salVAtion).
